title: Queen Windmill!
reviewNotes: Full six-piece physical diagram visually reconstructed: Ke8 Bc8 c7 versus Ke5 a3 b3. Source Bf5 offer, double promotion and checking circuit Qe6/Qe4/Qg4/Qg6/Qg7 produce a skewer and queen capture. Immediate Kxf5 allows promotion with check. Independent Kd4 Qf6+ comparison is explicit and keeps the queen out of king capture range. All seven contact sheets reviewed; small original frames were inspected directly.
transcript: The white bishop seems to be unable to stop the black pawns that are only a couple of squares away from getting new queens and it is blocking his own ally. So, the white king seems to be in a little bit of trouble here, but white has a sensational sequence that is going to allow him to win the game. And the first brilliant move that white needs to find is bishop to F5. A bishop sacrifice that aims at one of the promotion squares. And now, of course, if black carelessly captures this bishop, white is simply going to be able to promote the white pawn, get the new queen with a check and now it is going to be easy to stop the black pawns. But black is not that naive and he realizes that he can push the other pawn and now get only one square away from getting a new queen. And now it seems like both sides can get a queen and so this game is going to be headed towards a draw. But this is where we start to see the plan of white unfolding. The queen can now give a check to the king and force it to move below the bishop. If the king had moved to this square, it would have been on the same line as the queen and so after a check, we would have been able to pick up the black queen. So, the king goes to F4 and now white continues to chase it around with queen to E4 check. This time, if the king goes this way, it is actually going to pretty soon get checkmated by the queen and bishop. For example, with something like this. The king has to go here and now there is going to be a checkmate in just two more moves. But the king can, of course, keep on trying to hide behind the bishop, but that is what we want. We keep chasing the king around with another check. It cannot go here or it would get checkmated, but after it goes here, we still continue this windmill around the bishop and give another check like this. Now finally forcing the king onto a black square and on the same diagonal as the black queen, meaning that queen to G7 is going to be a check and a skewer. Once the king takes the bishop, we're going to be able to take this queen and very easily win the game. If you like this chessboard, read the first comment.
